newsitem.title: UK: UK's George says some further rate rise needed.
newsitem.headline: UK's George says some further rate rise needed.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George reiterated his view that some further rise in interest rates would be needed to prevent inflation taking off.

Asked by the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee if he thought policymakers were "ahead of the game" on monetary policy, he replied: "I think we were up with the game at the point when we raised interest rates in October."

"I would simply stand on the statement we made subsequently to that, which was that some further rate rise would be required at some point in order to give us a better than even chance of achieving the inflation target."
"All of that means we're not far off."
Asked about the extent and timing of the rate increases that might be required, George said: "It's jolly hard to say."

He could not say that June's quarter-point interest rate cut, which the Bank opposed, had been "a ghastly mistake" because he did not have sufficiently precise knowledge, but the decision had been debatable.
Adjusting monetary policy sooner rather than later meant any movement could be smaller rather than larger, George added.
